ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a regular hexagon and a regular pentagon are placed as depicted, with the common vertex $O$, and the side $AB$ of the hexagon and the side $DE$ of the pentagon lying on the same straight line. What is the measure of $\angle ABO$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution}: From what is given in the problem, we have $\angle ABO = \frac{1}{6} \times (6-2) \times 180^\circ = \boxed{120^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a regular hexagon, with the bottom side labeled AB; point B and point O are connected by one side, so A, B, O are consecutive vertices of this regular hexagon; on the right side is a regular pentagon, sharing vertex O with the regular hexagon, and AB and DE are on the same straight line. Reasoning: Because ∠ABO is the interior angle of the regular hexagon at vertex B, it is only necessary to calculate the interior angle of the regular hexagon. Each interior angle of a regular n-gon is ((n-2)×180°)/n. Taking n=6, obtain ((6-2)×180°)/6 = 120°. Therefore ∠ABO=120°.
